description: Colorado DL, layout taken from an issued credential. PII replaced.

provenance.source: PDF417 barcode decoded from a photo of the back of an issued Colorado driver's license, class R, REAL ID compliant (AAMVA v10, IIN 636020)
provenance.verifiedBy: Claude Code (zxing-cpp decode of the source image)
provenance.anonymization: Every identifying value was replaced with a placeholder of the same byte length and character class, so the encoded layout is byte-for-byte unchanged: DCS/DAC/DAD (names), DAQ (customer ID), DAG/DAI/DAK (address; DAK keeps a Colorado 8xxxx prefix and its two spaces of fill), DCF, and DBB/DBD/DBA (dates, shifted so expiry still falls on the birthday and validity stays inside Colorado's 5-year cap). DCJ keeps its CDOR_DL_0_ prefix; its MMDDYY date, which on the card fell one day after DBD, was shifted to stay one day after the shifted DBD, and its trailing five-digit number was zeroed. DDB (card revision date) describes the card stock rather than the holder and is unchanged, as are DCA/DCB/DCD/DBC/DAU/DAY/DAZ/DAW/DCL/DDA, the DDE/DDF/DDG truncation flags, and ZCA. expectedBytes was made by writing those placeholders into the decoded symbol in place, not by running this encoder; the header and directory are the card's own bytes.
provenance.notes: The symbol declares 332 bytes and holds 332: DL at offset 41 declaring 281, ZC at 322 declaring 10, both exactly contiguous, jurisdiction version 01. Four things the card had to be measured for, all now in Colorado's encoding profile: (1) the final element of each subfile is closed by the segment terminator alone, as New York does; (2) DAK is space-filled to the spec's F11 and DCL to the spec's F3 ('U' plus two spaces), and nothing else is padded; (3) DAU is written '065 in', with the unit in lower case exactly as the 2009 standard's own example ('073 in') writes it, where this generator otherwise upper-cases every standard string field; (4) a two-entry directory with a ZC subfile holding one element, ZCA, which read 'NONE'. ZC is not borrowed from Connecticut: the standard names a jurisdiction subfile 'Z' plus the first letter of the jurisdiction's name, so both states get ZC. The element order is the issuer's, not the schema's, and through DCG it is identical to the Connecticut card's (DAQ first, truncation flags interleaved with the names); after DCG Colorado writes DDA DDB DAZ DCJ DCL DAW and carries no DCK. Two schema gaps this card exposed: DCJ (audit information, V25ANS) was missing from every version's field table, and Colorado's field exclusions dropped DCL although the card carries it. The card also prints a Code 128 barcode reading an 11-digit number down its left edge; it is not part of the PDF417 payload and is not recorded here.
